caveats: ⚑ Demon's Breath status is kit-silent about its SOURCE. The burst line names 'Demon's Breath' as the self mode granted by her own burst, so skill1's 15-normal-attack stack counter is modeled as gated on that mode (declared via `modes`, default OFF-equivalent by the mode gate). If Demon's Breath is instead a battle-start/permanent self status, the gate is wrong and the ATK stack ramps from t=0 — measure whether her ATK climbs before her first burst.

⚑ skill1 ATK stack (4.22% × up to 30 = 126.6% max) is authored at MAX-stack magnitude with rampSec 8 as a stack-ramp haircut. The real trajectory is 15 MG rounds per stack; her MG cadence is datamine-unreliable so the true time-to-cap is unknown. Also unknown: whether each stack carries its OWN 10s timer (sawtooth, likely never reaching 30) or the whole pool refreshes — modeled as refresh-to-full, which OVER-CREDITS if per-stack.

⚑ Cadence tuple (MG 300 ammo / 171 reloadFrames / hitsPerShot 1 / normalAttackMultiplier 5.57) is datamined and unreliable; the hitCount:15 trigger counts ROUNDS, so the stack rate is directly downstream of it.

⚑ The healing/HP-sharing lines are encoded as heal EVENTS (no HP pool in v1) purely so any teammate's on-recovery trigger fires. Tick counts (10 / 180) are conventions for 'for 10 sec' and 'continuously over the 180s fight', not kit-stated.

⚑ skill2's second block targets 'self and 2 RL-wielding allies with the highest final ATK'. The schema has no 'self + top-N-by-weapon' target, so it is split: self is already covered by the first skill2 block's heal, and this block covers the 2 RL allies. It uses alliesOfWeapon (ALL RL allies), not a top-2 slice — over-targets if the team runs 3+ RL units. Since the heal carries no HP amount, the over-targeting moves no damage today, but it would over-fire on-recovery triggers.

⚑ Burst ATK line targets 'all allies with a Rocket Launcher' — reads as INCLUDING self if Rem were RL, but she is MG, so self is excluded naturally by the weapon filter. Left excludeSelf unset (the filter does the work).
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Rem is an MG/Water/Supporter/Burst II RL-enabler: her burst is a pure RL-team package (self crit + RL-only caster-scaled ATK + RL-only flat ammo), and her skill1 is a self ATK stack pool gated on the 'Demon's Breath' status her own burst names. Kit lines are 1:1 with blocks: skill1 = 15-normal-attack ATK stack (4.22% ×30) + a burst-cast team heal; skill2 = two continuous heal channels (self lifesteal, plus shared recovery with the 2 highest-ATK RL allies); burst = Demon's Breath crit self-buff + the RL ally ATK/ammo package. All heal/HP-sharing lines are modeled as recovery EVENTS rather than skipped — they are the tandem channel that drives a teammate's on-recovery consumer, and skipping them is the documented isolation trap. maxAmmoFlat 5 on RL allies is a real damage lever (an RL magazine is tiny, so +5 rounds is a large uptime change), not a defensive line.

flags.estimate: Demon's Breath = the self status granted by her own burst (10s window); skill1's stack counter only runs inside it
flags.reasoning: The status name appears in exactly one place in the whole kit — as the prefix on her burst's self crit line ('Demon's Breath: Critical Rate ▲ 37.8% for 10 sec'). The only structural read is that the burst GRANTS the status; skill1 then reads 'in Demon's Breath status' as a gate. The alternative (a battle-start permanent status the prose never grants) has no supporting line. Consequence is large: gated, the ATK pool can only build during ~10s post-burst windows and can plausibly never approach 30 stacks; ungated, it ramps from t=0 and caps early. This is the single highest-leverage unknown in the kit.
flags.recipe: Record a solo/enabled fight with DBG_BUFFS and read whether an atkPct buff on rem appears before her first burst cast. If ATK stacks appear from ~t=2s onward with no burst, the mode gate is wrong — drop `mode` and `modes`. If they appear only in 10s clusters starting at each burst cast, the gate is confirmed. A second, cheaper read: compare her own normal-attack popup magnitudes in the first 20s vs the 20s after her first burst.

flags.reasoning: 30 stacks × 15 landed rounds = 450 rounds to cap. Her belt is 300 with reloadFrames 171 (~2.85s), so a full belt plus most of a second is needed — but each stack lasts only 10s, so unless the pool refreshes as a whole, the tail stacks expire while the head is still building and 30 is unreachable. rampSec 8 is a mid estimate between 'caps almost instantly' and 'never caps'; it is NOT derived from a measured cadence because the MG cadence tuple is datamine-unreliable. Cross-check: 4.22 × 30 = 126.6% ATK is a very large self buff for a Supporter, which weakly suggests the real steady state sits well below cap.
flags.recipe: Two measurements. (1) Cadence: read her ammo counter across one full belt from footage to get true rounds/sec (never trust rate_of_fire). (2) Stack semantics: watch her buff icon stack number in footage — if it climbs monotonically to a plateau then drops to 0 all at once, the pool refreshes as a whole (current model); if it oscillates/sawtooths, each stack has its own timer and the model should switch to a steady-state haircut (~cap/2 or lower) instead of a ramp.

flags.estimate: whole-pool refresh (each new stack refreshes the 10s window on all stacks)
flags.reasoning: 'stacks up to 30 time(s) and lasts for 10 sec' is ambiguous between per-stack timers and a refreshing pool. The engine's maxStacks buff path is a refresh-to-full model, so the override inherits that. If the game runs per-stack timers, this model OVER-CREDITS: with per-stack expiry the pool can only hold as many stacks as she can generate in 10s.
flags.recipe: Same footage read as above — the buff-icon stack counter's decay shape is decisive (single cliff = refresh; staircase down = per-stack). No engine change needed if refresh is confirmed.

flags.estimate: alliesOfWeapon{weapon:'RL', excludeSelf:true} as a stand-in for 'self and 2 RL allies with the highest final ATK'
flags.reasoning: The schema has alliesOfWeapon (all, no count) and alliesTopAtk (count, no weapon filter) but no weapon+count intersection, and no self+allies composite. The split keeps self covered by the sibling block and covers RL allies without the top-2 slice. Because the effect is a heal with no HP amount, the over-targeting is damage-inert TODAY; it only matters if a 3rd RL ally is present AND some unit carries an on-recovery damage trigger.
flags.recipe: No measurement needed — this is a schema gap, not an empirical unknown. If a team ever runs 3+ RL units alongside a recovery-consumer (crown-style 'when recovery takes effect'), either extend TargetDef with an alliesOfWeapon count/byFinalAtk field or hard-restrict via alliesOfElementWeapon-style slicing. Record the limitation until then.

flags.estimate: 10 ticks for the 10s burst heal; 180 ticks for the two 'continuously' channels
flags.reasoning: The kit states durations ('for 10 sec', 'continuously') but no tick cadence. The engine's heal effect emits one recovery event per tick at intervalSec (default 1). 1/sec over the stated window is the neutral convention and matches how a continuous heal-over-time keeps an on-recovery consumer refreshed. 180 = the fight length. Neither number is kit-stated.
flags.recipe: Only matters if a teammate's on-recovery trigger is rate-sensitive. If a recovery-consumer's proc COUNT is ever popup-read in a team with rem, compare it against 1/sec and adjust intervalSec. Otherwise leave as convention.

Rem's whole skill1 stack rate is downstream of this, and MG wind-up further modulates early-fight rate.
